title: AI data centers are coming for federal land. They’re roiling the Nevada governor’s race
key_facts: The Townsite data center near Boulder City, Nevada, was the first in the country approved on federal public land, by the US Bureau of Land Management.
Residents beat an earlier plan on private land, the developers withdrew and sought adjacent federal land, and the Bureau of Land Management signed off.
Construction is stalled after a judge ruled the government could not use an old environmental review from when the project was meant to be a solar farm.
More than a dozen other data center projects on federal property are in the planning stages; 80 percent of Nevada's land is federally owned.
Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo does not outright oppose data centers on public land if communities support them; Democratic nominee Aaron Ford, the state attorney general, has pledged to oppose them.
Both say projects must follow state rules, such as covering their own energy costs and protecting water supplies, or lose state tax abatements.
UNLV political scientist David Damore called data centers a 'catalyzing issue' in the midterms; Texas Gov. Greg Abbott and Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro have also moved to restrict approvals.
President Trump, who backs the AI industry, signed an order last year to speed up permitting for AI data centers.
quote_evidence: The Townsite data center was the first in the country to be approved on federal public land, though construction is stalled after a judge ruled that the government couldn't use an old environmental review from when the project was intended to be a solar farm.
In Nevada, where 80% of the land is owned by the federal government, Townsite and other projects have become a dominant issue in the battleground state's closely watched governor's race.
Democratic nominee Aaron Ford, the state attorney general, has pledged to oppose data centers on public lands, saying affordable housing should be the priority.
why_it_matters_hint: Data centers on federal land can bypass local say, and in Nevada that has become a governor's race issue.
